endorsements.quote: Such is the importance of the training of medical imaging professionals, so as they are aware of the benefits and risks of AI’s use, that it should be both mandatory and free-of-charge to all who will benefit.

Along with education, emphasis should also be placed on raising awareness of AI and its applications starting from medical school, through radiology training as well as education courses for all healthcare workers, to make them aware and comfortable about the principles of AI as it can be applied to a clinical pathway, alongside safety and data governance topics.

AI needs to address the entire pathway—in the radiology lifecycle from referral management, vetting, prioritization, image acquisition, evaluation, and subsequent prioritization—and not implement interventions prematurely, which risks deterring potential users from adopting the technology.
The integration of AI into the workflow needs to be as seamless as possible to the user in order to maximize acceptance and uptake.

As such, national level test platforms would find a role here in helping to validate and monitor appropriate tools on a framework for delivery that can be used nationally, overcoming the limitations of Trusts that lack sufficient resources on a local level.

unlisted_practices: Establish national policy drive and national-level coordination between the NHS and industry for wide-scale AI adoption.
Generate prospective real-world evidence and robust health economic evaluations of AI tools, and maintain a national database of AI vendors and their evidence.
Conduct comparative studies of multiple AI products within the same modality to inform procurement decisions.
Minimize patient data leaving the NHS firewall, restrict AI access to the minimum data required, and de-identify patient data when sharing is necessary.
Include patient representatives on AI project innovation teams from the start.
Developers should ensure diverse datasets across ethnicities and geographies and continually evaluate and mitigate bias.
Monitor real-world AI performance throughout the whole lifecycle to ensure systems remain safe and effective.
Collect cost-effectiveness metrics alongside clinical outcomes when implementing or evaluating AI.
Digitize paper-based clinical records and improve IT infrastructure to enable AI integration.
Use change agents or ambassadors to drive the AI agenda across the organization.
